children: Indian rice export prices climbed to their highest level in over a year as concerns over production mounted due to below-average rainfall, while Thai rates edged lower and Vietnamese rates remained unchanged.

India's 5% broken parboiled variety (RI-INBKN5-P1) was quoted at $375-$381 per metric ton week, its highest level since July 2025, and up from the last week's $371-$377. Indian 5% broken white rice was priced at $372 to $377 per ton.
"Paddy prices in the local market are rising as traders expect a drop in production, which is effectively pushing up rice export prices as well," said New Delhi-based trader.

India's rice production is set to fall this year for the first time in a decade, and by the most in nearly 20 years, as below-normal rainfall during the crop's maturation period threatens to cut yields, industry officials told Reuters.
In Thailand, 5% broken rice prices (RI-THBKN5-P1) fell to $470 per ton from $488 last week, traders said.
Demand was weaker because importers have switched to other sources, traders said.
Traders also cited favorable weather in Thailand's northern and northeastern rice-growing regions, which was good news for the off-season rice, which will come out early next year, a trader said.
Vietnam's 5% broken rice (RI-VNBKN5-P1) was offered at $440-$445 per metric ton on Thursday, unchanged from a week ago.
"As summer-autumn harvest has come to an end, supplies have depleted. At the same time demand is soft as well, keeping the prices steady over the past weeks," said a trader based in Ho Chi Minh City.
"Although the Philippines is buying, demand for Vietnamese rice remains thin," the trader added.
In Bangladesh, domestic rice prices remained elevated despite ample supplies and sizeable government stockpiles.
